rules.label: Diarrhea
rules.recommendation: Hydration, replace electrolytes, Imodium, BRAT diet
rules.contactPhysicianWhen: Diarrhea lasting more than 2 days, signs of dehydration, fever of 102°F or higher, stools containing blood or pus

rules.label: Injection site reactions
rules.recommendation: Warm compress, ice pack, OTC pain medication, OTC allergy medication, movement
rules.contactPhysicianWhen: Keeps getting worse, lasts more than 1 to 2 days, signs of infection

rules.label: Eye and eyelid problems
rules.recommendation: Contact physician or optometrist as soon as possible; in the meantime, can try OTC artificial tears or OTC antihistamine drops
rules.contactPhysicianWhen: Contact physician as soon as possible

rules.label: Infections
rules.recommendation: Contact physician as soon as possible; can use OTC cold/flu medicine in the meantime
rules.contactPhysicianWhen: Contact physician as soon as possible

rules.label: Joint pain, muscle pain, or back pain
rules.recommendation: OTC pain relief, topical pain relief creams/patches, hot compress

triggerPhrases: trouble breathing after my last dose
rules.label: Reported allergic reaction
rules.recommendation: Advise holding the next dose until the prescriber is contacted; call 911 if breathing trouble or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat occurs

rules.label: Missed dose
rules.recommendation: Inject within 7 days of the missed dose and continue the original schedule; if more than 7 days, wait for the next scheduled dose
rules.description: Patient says they missed a dose

rules.label: Self-identify
rules.description: State your name, title, and where you're calling from

rules.label: Recording disclosure
rules.description: Tell the patient the call is being recorded

rules.label: Verify patient identity
rules.description: Confirm the patient's date of birth before discussing any PHI

rules.label: Review medication directions (SIG)
rules.description: Review the directions for use with the patient: dose, route, and how often

rules.label: Ask about medication list changes
rules.description: Ask whether anything on the patient's medication list has changed

rules.label: Ask about barriers to administration
rules.description: Ask whether the patient has any barriers or difficulty giving the medication (injection technique, cost, access, storage, refills)

rules.label: Ask about missed doses
rules.description: Ask whether the patient has missed any doses recently

rules.label: Closing: follow-up timeline
rules.description: Tell the patient when you will reach out again, and to call us if they have any questions

rules.label: Ask if the patient has any questions
rules.description: Ask whether the patient has any questions before ending the call

rules.label: Ask about ER visit / hospitalization
rules.description: Ask whether the patient has been to the ER or hospital recently (see G-02)

rules.label: Missed dose: adherence support
rules.description: If a missed dose is reported, the pharmacist should suggest ways to support adherence, such as alarms, pill boxes, and calendars. This appears as a pending checklist item, and if it is not covered by the end of the call, it is flagged as not covered

rules.label: Seriousness prompts
rules.description: Always ask about ER visits and hospitalization

rules.label: Patient's own attribution
rules.description: If the patient blames something else (food poisoning, a new supplement), record it as stated; do not decide causality

rules.label: Unmatched symptom
rules.description: If nothing matches, record the verbatim text and show "no rule matched; pharmacist to assess"

rules.label: Verbatim first
rules.description: The patient's exact words always stay in the note next to the standardized label
